stem: A 65 year-old male patient came with a distended abdomen, ascites and weight loss, after investigations it was found that he is having a cancer that is metastasizing to his lungs and there was an adherence within his bowels. The primary surgeon decided to perform an open palliative operation and upon taking the consent, the patient’s family refused open surgery and asked about the laparoscopic option. What would you tell the family about that choice ?

opts.t: No need because it’s palliative therapy and laparoscopy would be a waste of time and money
laparoscopy is contraindicated when there is no safe access
laparoscopy would be dangerous due to lung metastasis

srcNote: Source note (Midterm 439 A Q8): The related recall states: A. frozen abdomen is a contraindication. Answer: A.
expl: Dense adhesions between bowel loops (a "frozen" abdomen) mean there is no safe place to enter and create a working space — the real contraindication to laparoscopy here. Ascites and metastases alone are not contraindications.

why.A: Laparoscopy is often useful in palliation.
why.B: Ascites can be drained; it isn't a contraindication.

stem: Which of the following statements is true about laparoscopy?
expl: A frozen abdomen (dense adhesions) leaves no safe access — a contraindication. Laparoscopy isn't inferior and causes less post-operative pain.

why.B: For most operations it is equal or better.

stem: what pressure to maintain for laparoscopic pneumoperitoneum
expl: Pneumoperitoneum is kept at about 12–15 mmHg in adults — enough working space without impairing venous return and ventilation.

why.A: Too low for a good working space.
why.C: Higher than needed; more cardiorespiratory effects.

stem: A 32 year old lady is set to have a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Which of the following is the ideal pre-set pressure for the pneumoperitoneum?
expl: The usual pre-set insufflation pressure is 12 (to 15) mmHg.

why.B: Dangerous — compresses the IVC and splints the diaphragm.

stem: A 60-year old man, who is known diabetic and hypertensive admitted as a routine case for laparoscopic transabdominal right inguinal hernia repair under general anesthesia. After surgery the patient was transferred to the recovery room. Which of the following specifically need to be monitored?
srcNote: (Principles of laparoscopic surgery) (Surgical Complications) (THIS Q confused many students Bc in the previous years the Answer was B, but then we figured out based on our Marks that the right answer is A) The retained source notes a historical disagreement between answers A and B. Its stated key and original note are preserved.
expl: A diabetic hypertensive patient after GA is at risk of a (silent) perioperative MI → specifically monitor for MI. Students confirmed by their marks that the key is A (earlier years thought B).

why.B: Earlier assumed answer; airway is monitored for everyone.

stem: A patient came for a routine laparoscopic cholecystectomy, the surgeon explained to the patient that in order to do an abdominal procedure, carbon dioxide gas has to be used to insufflate the abdomen and create a space. The patient asked why do you use carbon dioxide. What would be your appropriate answer?

opts.t: It has a color and odor

expl: CO₂ is used because it is non-flammable, cheap and available in large amounts, and highly soluble (rapidly absorbed and exhaled). It is colourless and odourless.

why.B: It has no colour or odour.

stem: What’s the instrument used to introduce gas into the abdomen (pneumoperitoneum) to create the space to do laparoscopic procedure?
expl: The Veress needle — a spring-loaded blunt inner stylet in a sharp outer needle — is passed blindly into the peritoneum to insufflate CO₂ (closed technique).

stem: What are the main pillars of the laparoscopic tower?

opts.t: Gas insufflater, light source, and camera head with monitor
suction and irrigation, and camera head with monitor
long handle instruments, and camera head with monitor
long handle staples, and camera head with monitor

expl: The tower's essential units are the gas insufflator (creates the space), the light source (illuminates) and the camera head with monitor (shows the image).

why.C: Instruments aren't part of the tower.
why.D: Staplers aren't part of the tower.

stem: A 65 y/o male is planned to have a right hemicolectomy for colon cancer. Which of the following would have a beneficial effect on his metabolic response to surgery?

opts.t: Performing the surgery using a laparoscopic approach.
keeping the patient fasting for 3 days after surgery.

expl: The metabolic (stress) response is proportional to tissue injury. Laparoscopy reduces the trauma and therefore the catabolic/inflammatory response (an ERAS principle).

why.A: Paracetamol is analgesia; it doesn't modify the metabolic response meaningfully.
why.D: Prolonged fasting worsens catabolism; early feeding is recommended.

stem: In the picture shown below, from left to right, which of the following sentences is correct?

opts.t: Screen 1 shows the flow of gas
Screen 2 shows the pressure inside the abdomen
Screen 3 shows the remaining pressure in the tank
Screen 4 shows the pressure inside the abdomen

srcNote: (Principles of Laparoscopic surgery) (from right to left ( CO2 consumed - insufflation rate - intraabdominal pressure- how much left from the gas))
expl: On the insufflator, the displays from left to right are the gas-supply indicator, the intra-abdominal pressure (12 mmHg), the flow rate (15 L/min) and the volume of gas used (00.0 L) — so screen 2 shows the pressure inside the abdomen.

why.D: Screen 4 is the total gas volume used.

stem: Staplers Colors (Blue, white, green, black, etc) determine which of the following?
srcNote: (Principles of laparoscopic surgery) Source note (Midterm 435 A Q28): the Q may be about what does the color of the stapler indicates? It's the length of the staplers limb which depends on the thickness of the tissue. 2.5 --> vessel 3.5--> small bowel 5 --> stomach
expl: The colour of a stapler cartridge codes the staple leg (closed height) length, matched to tissue thickness — e.g. white 2.5 mm for thin/vascular tissue up to black 5 mm for thick tissue.

why.A: Line length is the cartridge length (e.g. 45 or 60 mm), not the colour.
why.B: The base (crown) width is the same.

stem: What is the maximum flow rate used in laparoscopic procedure to create a space by Veress needle?
expl: The Veress needle's narrow bore limits flow; initial insufflation is low (~1–2 L/min) until correct intraperitoneal placement is confirmed by low pressures — the source key is 2 L/min.

stem: Identify the device shown (a generator with hand instruments).
srcNote: (Principles of Laparoscopic surgery) Incomplete recall: the source has no written question stem, and option D is blank.
expl: The picture shows an energy generator with sealing/dividing hand pieces — a vessel sealing system (e.g. LigaSure).

why.B: A Veress needle is a single insufflation needle.
why.C: A light source has a fibre-optic cable, not hand instruments.

stem: Which of the following sizes is NOT available regarding veress needle?
expl: Veress needles come in lengths of about 80–150 mm (8–15 cm) for different abdominal wall thicknesses; a 40-cm needle doesn't exist.

stem: Which of the following is correct:
expl: In the pictured tower, unit 4 is the light source (the other units are the monitor, camera control and insufflator).

stem: What does NOTES stand for?
srcNote: (Principles of Laparoscopic Surgery) Incomplete choice set: options B, C and D are blank in the source.
ansText: Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery — reaching the peritoneal cavity through a natural orifice (stomach, vagina, rectum, bladder) without a skin incision.

stem: Site of monitor for appendectomy?
expl: The monitor is placed opposite the surgeon, in line with the target: for an appendectomy the surgeon stands on the patient's left looking towards the right iliac fossa, so the monitor goes on the patient's right.

stem: Why do we use carbon dioxide in laparoscopic procedures?

opts.t: It is not toxic, inert, and easily soluble
It is expensive and not available
It has a color and odor

expl: CO₂ is non-toxic, relatively inert (non-flammable) and highly soluble in blood — so it is safe with diathermy and a gas embolus is quickly absorbed.

why.B: It is cheap and widely available.

stem: While you're in 453 surg course, you attended laparoscopic appendectomy and the surgeon complained that there is no gas. The nurse went to bring another gas tank, your fellow intern told you to connect the oxygen tank. What would tell him?

opts.t: Sorry I will use anesthesia nitrous oxide instead
Sorry I will use room air instead

srcNote: (Principles of laparoscopic surgery) gas traits: not inflammable like oxygen’ Dr notes
expl: Laparoscopy needs a non-flammable, highly soluble gas — CO₂. Oxygen supports combustion (diathermy fire) and can embolize; nitrous oxide supports combustion and room air risks fatal air embolism.

why.C: N₂O supports combustion — unsafe with diathermy.
why.D: Room air (nitrogen) is poorly soluble → gas embolism.

stem: What is the difference between Harmonic scalpel and Ligasure?

opts.t: Harmonic scalpel is Bipolar is Ligasure is Ultrasonic
Harmonic scalpel is Electrocautery Legasure is Ultrasonic
Harmonic scalpel is Ultrasonic Ligasure is Bipolar
Harmonic scalpel is Electrocautery Ligasure is Bipolar

expl: The Harmonic scalpel uses ultrasonic vibration to cut and coagulate; LigaSure is an advanced bipolar vessel-sealing device.

stem: What is the safest trocar to be used?
expl: Blunt, bladeless (conical/optical) trocar tips push tissue apart rather than cutting it — the safest, with fewer vessel and bowel injuries and smaller fascial defects. Sharp pyramidal or bladed tips are the most dangerous.

why.D: Conical, but the source key is pic 3.

stem: What is the incisional inside that uses natural orifice surgeries?
srcNote: (Principles of Laparoscopic surgery) transgastric, transrectal, transvaginal (dr Qahtani book)
expl: NOTES reaches the peritoneal cavity through a natural orifice — transgastric, transvaginal, transrectal or transvesical; transrectal is the only natural-orifice route offered.

stem: A 33-year old woman admitted as gallstones for day case laparoscopic cholecystectomy. After surgery the patient was transferred to the ward. Which of the following is needed to be assessed during the post-operative?
srcNote: (Surgical Complications) Source note (Midterm 430 A Q89): The first postoperative-day version asks what is included in care and gives C. Clinical assessment. Answer: C.
expl: After a lap chole the first thing to assess on the ward is cardio-respiratory status (airway, breathing, circulation after anesthesia). Port-site hernia, infection and wound problems appear later.
